comments.body:
PRIOR-ART SEARCH — this is NOT a regression. Two earlier fixes in the same subsystem were checked and
BOTH are verifiably still in place. Recording this so nobody re-derives it, and — more importantly —
so nobody tries to fix this one the way those were fixed, because that approach cannot work here.

SEARCHED: "no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event", "plan_relation_snapshot_error", "reducer-error",
"empty ticket directory", "plan relation snapshot failed".

CANDIDATE 1 — fa77-b035-8541-4763 (CLOSED) "Plan relation snapshots reject rebar runtime marker files".
Closest match by subsystem. It fixed per-ticket `.archived` and `.write.lock` runtime markers making
the store permanently git-DIRTY, so `tracker_head_sha` rejected it and every plan review returned an
unsigned INDETERMINATE store-read-failure. Remedy: add those patterns to the tickets-branch gitignore.
VERIFIED STILL IN PLACE: `*/.archived` and `*/.write.lock` are both present in the tickets-branch
`.gitignore`; the markers exist on disk (e.g. `f2dc-cfff-cf06-483e/.write.lock`, `.../.archived`);
`git status --porcelain` on the tracker is CLEAN. Not regressed.

CANDIDATE 2 — c083-4d7d-0aca-4e3f (CLOSED) "sign-review fails on stray untracked tracker files:
attest.py omits ignore_untracked". Same theme, git-visibility again.
VERIFIED STILL IN PLACE: `ignore_untracked` is present at
`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py:208,212,242`. Not regressed.

WHY NEITHER FIX COULD EVER HAVE COVERED THIS, and why the gitignore route is a dead end here:
both prior fixes work by making git IGNORE an artifact it can otherwise SEE. Git cannot track empty
directories at all — an event-less ticket directory never appears in `git status`, never reaches the
tickets branch, and cannot be gitignored because there is nothing for git to ignore. Confirmed
directly: with the two orphan directories present, `git status --porcelain` was clean and the failure
still occurred. So this is a different failure mode reached by a different path — the REDUCER walking
the store directory listing, not git reporting dirtiness — and it needs a fix in the reducer, not in
`.gitignore`.

THE PATTERN WORTH NAMING: three separate tickets now (fa77, c083, this one) all reduce to "the
plan-review path is intolerant of store detritus and fails closed on an unrelated ticket". Each was
fixed for its specific artifact. Whoever takes this one should consider whether the reducer should
tolerate ANY unreadable/incomplete store entry by skipping it with a named warning, rather than
accruing a fourth case-by-case fix.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
AC3 DECISION RECORDED — the WRITER is NOT changed; the fix is reader-side tolerance only.

Decision: `_store/event_append._prepare_event` keeps creating the ticket directory BEFORE its
first event (`os.makedirs(ticket_dir, exist_ok=True)`), and the plan-relation reducer tolerates
the resulting event-less directory instead. The reasoning is recorded as a code comment at that
exact makedirs site so it is not re-litigated.

Reasoning, three independent reasons:

1. A writer-side cleanup CANNOT cover the observed failure mode. The write path is makedirs ->
   stage temp -> under-lock atomic rename. The orphans we found came from PROCESS DEATH
   (crash/kill/timeout) inside that window; a best-effort rmdir on the staging-failure path only
   closes the narrow subset that already raises a Python exception, and leaves the actual
   mechanism intact.
2. Cleanup is UNSAFE under this store's concurrency model. Many sessions write one shared
   .tickets-tracker. Removing a directory another session just created races its in-flight write.
   This is the same 'tolerate, never tidy' rule already established for stray .tmp-event-* files
   (see test_resign_tolerates_a_concurrent_writer_churning_tracker_temp_files).
3. Only the reader-side fix REPAIRS EXISTING BROKEN CLONES. A writer change does nothing for a
   clone already carrying an orphan — and since git cannot track empty directories, such a clone
   cannot be repaired by pulling either.

Scope of the tolerance is deliberately NARROW and mutation-proven in both directions:
* event-less directory -> skipped with a WARNING naming the absolute path (RED before the fix
  reproduced the exact reported signature: reason=reducer-error reference=0de5-6db1-8058-4e80).
* directory that DOES hold events but still fails to reduce -> still raises reducer-error, so a
  genuinely corrupt ticket that may carry relation material never gets silently dropped. Proven
  by mutating _holds_no_events to `return True`: the narrowness test then FAILS with
  'DID NOT RAISE PlanRelationSnapshotError'.

Commit: a30dc6c22b (branch fix/043f-84aa-infra; NOT pushed to Gerrit per instruction).

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

A ticket directory containing NO events — created by a write that never emitted its CREATE event —
makes the plan-relation reducer error out, and that error surfaces as an INDETERMINATE verdict on
plan reviews of OTHER, UNRELATED tickets. The blast radius is every ticket whose relation graph the
snapshot walks, which in practice means an entire epic.

## Reproduced, then fixed, by removing the directory and nothing else

Running `rebar review-plan 5267-f026-0f2b-4c02`:

    verdict INDETERMINATE, exit 2, llm_ran: FALSE
    indeterminate[0] = {id: plan-relation-snapshot-error, reason: reducer-error,
                        canonical_id: None, reference: 0de5-6db1-8058-4e80}
    ERROR rebar.llm.plan_review: plan relation snapshot failed

`0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` was an EMPTY DIRECTORY in `.tickets-tracker` — `ls -A` returned 0 entries,
`rebar show` reported `has no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event`. A second one, `4ab3-411d-9736-4a41`, was in
the same state.

CRITICALLY, 5267 DOES NOT REFERENCE 0de5. Its only dep is `relates_to 208f-6e90-1326-403a`; the
broken directory was reached by walking the epic's relation graph. A grep across the whole store for
`0de5-6db1-8058-4e80` returned ZERO references from any ticket — nothing points at it at all.

After removing the two empty directories and changing nothing else, the SAME command on the SAME tree
returned `verdict: PASS`, exit 0, attestation certified at ff295b9cf87. That is the causal proof: one
variable changed.

## Why this is worth fixing rather than sweeping

* It is NOT transient. An earlier agent on this epic hit the same signature and recorded it as
  "transient store churn from a half-written ticket, retried clean". It is not churn — it persists
  until someone removes the directory, and a retry only appears to work if the racing writer happens
  to complete in the interim.
* The error names the BROKEN ticket, not the one being reviewed, so the failure looks like a problem
  with an unrelated ticket. That is a strong wrong-direction signal for anyone debugging it.
* It is invisible to git. Git cannot track empty directories, so the artifact never appears in
  `git status`, never reaches the tickets branch, and cannot be spotted by inspecting the shared
  history — it exists only in a local clone.
* The LLM never runs (`llm_ran: false`), so the gate fails closed with no spend. That is correct
  behaviour, but it means the whole epic's claims and closes stall on a filesystem artifact.

## Approach (not yet decided)

The reducer should tolerate a ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event rather than failing the
whole snapshot — most plausibly by skipping it with a warning naming the path, since a directory with
no events carries no information that a relation snapshot needs. Consider also whether the writer can
avoid creating the directory before it has an event to put in it, which would remove the artifact at
source.

Both directions should be weighed; tolerating the artifact is the smaller, safer change and fixes
existing broken clones, while fixing the writer prevents new ones and does nothing for clones already
carrying one.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A ticket directory with no CREATE/SNAPSHOT event does not fail the plan-relation snapshot; the
      review proceeds and the artifact is reported as a warning naming the offending path.
- [ ] A test constructs an event-less ticket directory and asserts `review-plan` on an UNRELATED
      ticket still reaches a verdict; it fails before the fix.
- [ ] It is decided and recorded whether the writer should also stop creating the directory before it
      has an event to write, with the reasoning either way.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
compiled_state.title: An event-less ticket directory fails the plan-relation reducer, turning unrelated plan reviews INDETERMINATE
